correctness.rationale: In Euclidean coordinates the sigma-admissibility inequality is exactly |y-cx|<=s|x|sqrt(sigma^2-1). Independent conditional uniform choices therefore factor each sweep as X_{n+1}=X_n(c+sU_n)(c+sV_n). The exact second-moment and general p-moment integrals follow by elementary integration; the strict mean-square barrier uses c^2+s^2=1. For r>0 the log multipliers have finite second moments and nonzero variance, giving the SLLN, while the LIL excludes convergence at zero log drift. Analytic integration and the derivative (1-t artanh(t))/r establish a single root and the strict hierarchy by Jensen. The bundled code verifies rational parameter expansions and log-root signs but is not the proof.

value.rationale: Quasioptimal projection methods permit a range of legal errors but deterministic worst-case convergence alone does not quantify the behavior of a symmetric randomized selection. The exact angle-independent mean-square cutoff sigma=2 contrasts with the angle-dependent robust and almost-sure cutoffs and supplies a crisp performance/reliability separation: a.s. iterates can vanish although expected squared residuals diverge. This is a natural, fully specified stochastic oracle benchmark with clear limitations and an exact all-p moment profile, not an arbitrary numerical slice or a restatement of a deterministic theorem.
